statements.t: We are also focused on maximizing the value of our land, mineral ownership, and energy expertise for decarbonization by developing carbon capture and storage (CCS) and other emissions-reducing projects.
We expect oil prices to remain volatile as these geopolitical circumstances continue to evolve.
We expect these prices to impact our full year 2026 costs by approximately $10 million.
We also expect higher energy prices to continue to affect our results in 2027.

Until this matter is resolved or additional transportation capacity becomes available, we expect reduced capacity on this pipeline segment to continue to negatively impact our realizations and transportation costs.
We do not expect this settlement to materially affect our future price realizations or volumes sold.
We continue to dispute the validity of the force majeure claim made by the other counterparty and expect to submit the dispute to arbitration later this year.

The litigation challenges Kern County’s certification of the revised environmental impact report (REIR) prepared under CEQA for our Carbon TerraVault I CCS project at our Elk Hills field, and the County’s related approval of the project.
This REIR underlies our CTV I project and impacts the CEQA analysis for the potential CalCapture project.
However, we are developing multiple other CTV projects that do not rely on this REIR.
We intend to aggressively pursue legal actions to protect and advance our CTV I project; however, we can provide no assurances that we will be successful in these efforts.

We currently expect the EPA to issue draft permits for certain of these projects by year-end 2026; however, the timing remains uncertain, and we cannot provide assurances as to if or when the permits will be issued.
As of September 30, 2026, we have hedges on approximately 65% of our expected oil production for the remainder of 2026 at a weighted average floor price of $64.80.
Our carbon management segment, which we refer to as Carbon TerraVault, is engaged in the operation and development of CCS projects.
We completed construction of our first carbon capture project at our cryogenic gas processing facility and achieved our first injection during the second quarter of 2026.

We expect that our Carbon TerraVault business will develop other CCS projects using CO 2 captured from industrial, power, agriculture and other emissions sources into subsurface reservoirs and permanently store CO 2 deep underground.
We may also participate in the ownership and development of projects that are the source of these CO 2 emissions.
The amounts related to carbon management projects do not include amounts funded by Brookfield through the Carbon TerraVault JV, such as drilling injection and monitoring wells at our 26R reservoir.
We expect to enter 2027 with 6 rigs in California.
We will continue to evaluate our hedging strategy based on prevailing market prices and conditions.
